prompts:
Use case: illustration-story. A production NINE-FRAME animation sprite atlas, 3 columns by3 rows, square canvas, genuine transparent background.
REFERENCE1: primary exact character. Its TOP-LEFT bird is the canonical resting Korean magpie: small rounded head, thin softly pointed beak, small round white eye, plump white belly with a thin dark outline, folded wing with oval white patch, long slender tail upward45 degrees. REFERENCE2: supporting consistency reference only.
Create a SMALL VERTICAL TWO-FOOT HOP in place, NOT flying and NOT a walking step. Draw9 COMPLETE coherent birds, all facing LEFT, same scale, same head size/beak/eye/torso volume. Numbering only for prompt, DO NOT put labels in image:
0 Almost identical to reference1 TOP-LEFT neutral bird. Both feet planted, starting to bend knees just a tiny amount.
1 Gentle preparation: both knees bend, head and chest lower slightly, tail tilts a few degrees for balance; body shape remains same cute bird.
2 Deepest small crouch: both legs visibly folded, torso lowered modestly toward heels, same head and belly dimensions, wings still folded, tail balances slightly higher.
3 Push-off halfway: legs unfold and ankle joints straighten, chest rises; both toe tips still meet a common ground plane.
4 Toe spring: both legs extended downward, heels raised, only toe tips touch; body slightly taller because legs extended, NOT resized; tiny wing opening for balance.
5 Rising in air: feet begin folding underneath, curled toes no longer on ground, wings subtly lifted only15 degrees, tail angles modestly downward relative to back.
6 Apex: both feet neatly tucked under belly, toes curled, wings subtly away from sides, body comfortably rounded, same size.
7 Descending: both feet extend toward ground, toes spread for landing, wings beginning to close; same body and head size.
8 First soft toe contact: both toes meet the same baseline, knees beginning to bend, wings folded and tail returning to reference angle. This pose leads naturally back through frame1 and reference neutral.
CRITICAL the change is anatomical whole-bird posture, not moving a rigid cutout. Keep the SAME beak and rounded head profile and the SAME eye-to-beak distance in every drawing. Tiny neck/torso rotations only; head stays level left-facing, not upward. Never enlarge or shrink the head or body. Stable foot spacing for grounded poses. No walking, no raised huge flight wings, no extra feet. Keep full long tails with generous transparent gutters around each bird, no overlapping cells or cropping. All frames consistent proportions with reference1. Charcoal #2e2a26 and white patches only. No gray glow, shadow, floor, motion lines, numbers, text, scenery or other elements.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit only THREE tail angles in this nine-frame magpie sprite sheet. Preserve every head, beak, eye, torso, white patch, wing, leg, toe, canvas position, scale and transparency exactly.
The airborne tails currently swing abruptly downward, which will pop in animation. Make the long tails in these cells point gently UPWARD toward the right instead:
MIDDLE ROW RIGHT (frame5): tail points30 degrees upward-right.
BOTTOM ROW LEFT (frame6): tail points24 degrees upward-right.
BOTTOM ROW MIDDLE (frame7): tail points33 degrees upward-right.
These angles are measured from horizontal; positive upward. The other six tails are unchanged. Retain the same slender tail length and two rounded feather tips. Redraw the root connection smoothly where tail meets rump, no duplicate stump or protruding remnants. Keep generous transparent gutters without touching neighboring birds. Do not shift or scale any birds. All other artwork stays EXACTLY unchanged. True transparent background, no glow or shadow.
packing: cwebp -lossless -exact -z 9; retain original PNG as editable source
design: Nine whole-bird poses: near-rest, bend, deep crouch, leg extension, toe spring, partial tuck, apex tuck, leg reach, soft contact. Two hops reuse them with an anticipation and recovery sequence.
continuity: One scale0.224 across all poses; canonical eye aperture and beak core. Source soles anchor grounded poses. In the air, continuous head registration bridges leg drawings without changing the body's scale.
